framework.title: Life Insurer Benchmarking Framework (India)
framework.summary: Fifteen pillars that mirror how a life insurer is organised, from the board's view of scale and value down to the departments that sell, price, underwrite, pay claims, serve customers and run technology. Each pillar holds KPIs with a definition, formula, direction, source and refresh frequency. Core KPIs feed the scores; context KPIs explain the mix without ranking it.

scoring.method: Within each core KPI, insurers with a value are ranked and given a percentile score from 0 (worst) to 100 (best), flipped where lower is better. A pillar score is the average of the insurer's core KPI scores in that pillar, shown only when at least 2 are available. The overall index averages the scored pillars (equal weights) and is shown only when at least 6 pillars are scored.
caveats: Scores rank insurers against each other; they are not ratings of financial soundness.
Business mix drives many ratios (a single-premium or group-heavy book reads differently from a regular-premium retail book). Compare within peer groups for fairness.
Each KPI shows its period. Where sources publish at different times, a KPI uses one source for all insurers so periods match.

peer_groups.name: Same size tier
peer_groups.rule: NBP market share, financial year to date: Leader 10%+, Large 3-10%, Mid 1-3%, Small 0.3-1%, Emerging below 0.3%

peer_groups.name: Same distribution model
peer_groups.rule: From individual new business premium by channel: Agency-led (agents 50%+), Banca-led (bank partners 50%+), Direct-led (direct and online 40%+), otherwise Multi-channel

irdai_monthly.name: IRDAI monthly New Business Statement of Life Insurers

irdai_handbook.name: IRDAI Handbook on Indian Insurance Statistics

ombudsman.name: Council for Insurance Ombudsmen annual report

catalogue.name: This dashboard's product catalogue (insurers' product lists and brochures)

app_stores.name: Google Play and Apple App Store listings

web_audit.name: Homepage audit run by this project

pillars.name: Scale & market position
pillars.question: How big is the franchise and how much of the market does it hold?

kpis.name: New business premium, year to date
kpis.def: First-year plus single premium collected this financial year to date, individual and group.
kpis.why: The headline measure of selling power.

kpis.name: Share of industry new business
kpis.def: Insurer's new business premium as a share of all life insurers, year to date.
kpis.why: Relative position, independent of market cycles.

kpis.name: Share of private-sector new business
kpis.def: New business premium as a share of the private insurers' total, year to date (not shown for LIC).
kpis.why: The fight that matters for private insurers.

kpis.name: Individual new business premium, year to date
kpis.def: Individual single plus non-single first-year premium, year to date.
kpis.why: Retail franchise strength, without lumpy group fund flows.

kpis.name: Share of industry individual new business
kpis.def: Individual new business premium as a share of the industry's, year to date.

kpis.name: Total premium (gross written)
kpis.def: First-year, single and renewal premium for the financial year.
kpis.why: Size of the in-force book plus new sales.

kpis.name: Assets under management
kpis.def: Investments across life, pension and group, and unit-linked funds at 31 March.
kpis.why: Balance-sheet scale and long-term earnings base.

kpis.name: Individual policies in force
kpis.def: Individual policies in force at 31 March, all lines of business.
kpis.why: Size of the customer base to serve and cross-sell.

kpis.name: Sum assured written, year to date
kpis.def: Sum assured on new business this financial year to date.

kpis.name: Group lives covered, year to date
kpis.def: Lives covered under new group schemes this financial year to date.
kpis.why: Reach of group and credit-life business.

pillars.name: Growth momentum
pillars.question: Is it gaining or losing ground?

kpis.name: New business premium growth, year to date
kpis.def: Year-to-date new business premium against the same period last year.

kpis.name: Individual new business growth, year to date
kpis.def: Year-to-date individual new business premium against the same period last year.

kpis.name: Individual regular-premium growth, year to date
kpis.def: Year-to-date individual non-single premium against the same period last year.
kpis.why: Growth in the most valuable, recurring business.

kpis.name: Individual policies sold, growth
kpis.def: Year-to-date individual policies issued against the same period last year.
kpis.why: Customer acquisition, not just ticket size.

kpis.name: Change in market share
kpis.def: Year-to-date share of industry new business minus the same period last year, in basis points.
kpis.why: Winning or losing against the market.

kpis.name: Latest month new business growth
kpis.def: New business premium in the latest month against the same month last year.

kpis.name: Total premium growth
kpis.def: Total premium against the previous financial year.
kpis.why: Growth of the whole book, including renewals.

kpis.name: Total premium growth, 3-year CAGR
kpis.def: Compound annual growth of total premium over three financial years.

kpis.name: AUM growth
kpis.def: Assets under management against a year earlier.
kpis.why: Compounding of the balance sheet (includes market movements).

pillars.name: Profitability & value creation
pillars.question: Does growth create value for shareholders and policyholders?

kpis.name: Profit after tax
kpis.def: Shareholders' profit after tax for the financial year.
kpis.why: Accounting profit (understates value for growing insurers).

kpis.name: Return on equity
kpis.def: Profit after tax divided by average shareholders' funds.

kpis.name: Profit after tax to premium
kpis.def: Profit after tax divided by total premium.

kpis.name: Policyholders' account surplus to premium
kpis.def: Surplus (deficit) in the policyholders' account divided by premium.
kpis.why: Whether the insurance operations generate surplus before shareholder support.

kpis.name: Shareholders' funds (net worth)
kpis.def: Share capital, reserves and surplus and fair value change, at 31 March.

kpis.name: Net worth growth
kpis.def: Shareholders' funds against a year earlier.

kpis.name: VNB margin
kpis.def: Value of new business as a share of annualised premium equivalent, as reported by the insurer.
kpis.why: Economic profitability of new sales; published mainly by listed insurers.

pillars.name: Capital, risk & investments
pillars.question: Is the balance sheet safe and the money well managed?

kpis.name: Solvency ratio
kpis.def: Available solvency margin divided by required solvency margin at the latest quarter end in the source (IRDAI's control level is 1.5).
kpis.why: Capital cushion; very high levels can also mean idle capital.

kpis.name: Solvency change over 4 quarters
kpis.def: Latest solvency ratio minus the ratio four quarters earlier.

kpis.name: Unit-linked share of AUM
kpis.def: Unit-linked funds as a share of total assets under management.

kpis.name: AUM to total premium
kpis.def: Assets under management divided by total premium.
kpis.why: Maturity and savings depth of the book.

kpis.name: Reinsurance ceded to premium
kpis.def: Premium ceded to reinsurers divided by gross premium.
kpis.why: How much mortality risk is passed on.

kpis.name: Investment yield
kpis.def: Yield on policyholders' and shareholders' investments without unrealised gains (form L-34).

kpis.name: Gross NPA in investments
kpis.def: Gross non-performing investments as a share of total (form L-33).

pillars.name: Distribution & sales
pillars.question: How diversified and productive is the sales engine?

kpis.name: Agency share of individual new business
kpis.def: Individual new business premium sold by individual agents, share of total.
kpis.why: Reliance on a proprietary agency force.

kpis.name: Bancassurance share
kpis.def: Individual new business premium through bank corporate agents, share of total.

kpis.name: Other corporate agents share
kpis.def: Individual new business premium through non-bank corporate agents (NBFCs, MFIs and others), share of total.

kpis.name: Broker share
kpis.def: Individual new business premium through brokers, share of total.

kpis.name: Direct and online share
kpis.def: Individual new business premium from direct selling and online, share of total.

kpis.name: POSP, web aggregators and others
kpis.def: Individual new business premium through point-of-sale persons, web aggregators, insurance marketing firms, micro-insurance agents, common service centres and others.

kpis.name: Channel diversity index
kpis.def: 100 x (1 - sum of squared channel shares of individual new business premium). 0 = one channel only.
kpis.why: Resilience: less dependence on any single partner or channel.

kpis.name: Individual agents
kpis.def: Licensed individual agents at 31 March.
kpis.why: Size of the proprietary sales force.

kpis.name: Agent force growth
kpis.def: Individual agents against a year earlier.

kpis.name: New business premium per agent
kpis.def: Average individual new business premium per individual agent.

kpis.name: Policies per agent
kpis.def: Average individual policies sold per individual agent.

kpis.name: Corporate agent partners
kpis.def: Corporate agents (banks and others) tied to the insurer at 31 March.

kpis.name: Offices
kpis.def: Offices across states and union territories at 31 March.

kpis.name: New business premium per office
kpis.def: Annual new business premium divided by offices.

kpis.name: States and UTs with individual business
kpis.def: States and union territories where the insurer wrote individual new business premium.

kpis.name: Top-3 states share of individual business
kpis.def: Share of individual new business premium from the insurer's three largest states.

kpis.name: Average individual premium per policy
kpis.def: Year-to-date individual new business premium divided by individual policies.
kpis.why: Customer segment and channel mix (affluent versus mass).

kpis.name: Regular premium share of individual business
kpis.def: Individual non-single premium as a share of individual new business premium, year to date.
kpis.why: Quality of the retail book: recurring premiums build value.

kpis.name: Individual share of new business
kpis.def: Individual new business premium as a share of the insurer's total new business premium, year to date.

pillars.name: Product & proposition
pillars.question: How broad, fresh and accessible is the shelf?

kpis.name: Individual products on sale
kpis.def: Individual plans currently on sale.

kpis.name: Categories covered
kpis.def: How many of the six individual categories (term, ULIP, par savings, non-par savings, pension and annuity, health and CI) have at least one plan on sale.
kpis.why: Completeness of proposition across life stages.

kpis.name: Products launched in 12 months
kpis.def: New individual products launched in the last 12 months, from the change log.

kpis.name: Products and riders filed in the year
kpis.def: Products and riders filed with IRDAI during the financial year (File & Use plus Use & File).

kpis.name: Riders on sale
kpis.def: Riders currently offered.

kpis.name: Group products on sale
kpis.def: Group plans currently on sale (term, credit life, gratuity, superannuation, annuity and others).

kpis.name: Plans buyable online
kpis.def: Share of individual plans on sale that can be bought online.

kpis.name: IRDAI standard products offered
kpis.def: Standard products on sale (Saral Jeevan Bima, Saral Pension and others).

kpis.name: Micro-insurance products
kpis.def: Micro-insurance products on sale.

kpis.name: ULIP share of new business
kpis.def: Linked new business premium as a share of total new business premium.

kpis.name: Protection intensity of retail sales
kpis.def: Sum assured on individual new business per rupee of individual new business premium, year to date.
kpis.why: How much life cover the retail book actually sells.

kpis.name: Longest term cover offered
kpis.def: Highest maturity age across term plans on sale.
kpis.why: Competitiveness of the flagship protection product.

pillars.name: Marketing & brand
pillars.question: How visible and well regarded is the brand?

kpis.name: News mentions, last 30 days
kpis.def: Headlines naming the insurer in Google News (India) over 30 days.

kpis.name: Share of voice
kpis.def: Insurer's news mentions as a share of mentions of all tracked insurers, 30 days.

kpis.name: App installs (Android)
kpis.def: Lower bound of the Google Play install range for the customer app.
kpis.why: Reach of the brand's digital front door.

kpis.name: App ratings given
kpis.def: Ratings on Google Play and the App Store combined.

kpis.name: Review-site rating
kpis.def: Average customer rating on review and aggregator sites.
kpis.why: Reputation outside the insurer's own channels.

kpis.name: Social platforms linked
kpis.def: Social networks linked from the homepage (Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, YouTube, X).

kpis.name: Advertisement & publicity to premium
kpis.def: Advertisement and publicity expense divided by total premium (schedule L-6).

pillars.name: Underwriting & risk selection
pillars.question: Does it select risk well without denying genuine claims?

kpis.name: Death claims repudiated (by number)
kpis.def: Individual death claims repudiated divided by total claims for the year.
kpis.why: High repudiation points to weak underwriting at entry or a tough claims stance.

kpis.name: Death claims repudiated (by amount)
kpis.def: Amount of individual death claims repudiated divided by total claim amount.

kpis.name: Death claims rejected
kpis.def: Individual death claims rejected (outside policy terms) divided by total claims.

kpis.name: Group death claims repudiated
kpis.def: Group death claims repudiated divided by total group claims.
kpis.why: Risk selection in group and credit-life business.

kpis.name: Mortality experience (actual vs expected)
kpis.def: Actual claims as a share of claims expected in pricing, where disclosed.
kpis.why: Direct test of underwriting quality; disclosed by few insurers.

pillars.name: Claims
pillars.question: Does it pay, and pay fast?

kpis.name: Death claims paid (by number)
kpis.def: Individual death claims paid divided by total claims (pending at start plus intimated).

kpis.name: Death claims paid (by amount)
kpis.def: Amount of individual death claims paid divided by total claim amount.
kpis.why: Shows whether large claims are paid as readily as small ones.

kpis.name: Death claims settled within 30 days
kpis.def: Individual death claims settled within 30 days of intimation, share of claims settled.
kpis.why: Speed at the moment that matters most.

kpis.name: Death claims pending at year end
kpis.def: Individual death claims pending at year end divided by total claims.

kpis.name: Group death claims paid
kpis.def: Group death claims paid divided by total group claims.
kpis.why: Claims performance for employer and credit-life members.

kpis.name: Death claims paid, latest disclosed
kpis.def: Most recent claim settlement ratio by number as compiled from insurer disclosures.
kpis.why: A more recent read than the IRDAI handbook.

pillars.name: Customer service & retention
pillars.question: Do customers stay, and are they treated well?

kpis.name: 13th-month persistency
kpis.def: Share of policies (by number) still in force at the 13th month, at 31 March.
kpis.why: Sales quality: mis-sold policies lapse early.

kpis.name: 25th-month persistency
kpis.def: Share of policies (by number) still in force at the 25th month.

kpis.name: 37th-month persistency
kpis.def: Share of policies (by number) still in force at the 37th month.

kpis.name: 49th-month persistency
kpis.def: Share of policies (by number) still in force at the 49th month.

kpis.name: 61st-month persistency
kpis.def: Share of policies (by number) still in force at the 61st month.

kpis.name: 13th-month persistency, 5-year change
kpis.def: 13th-month persistency now minus five years earlier, in percentage points.

kpis.name: Lapse ratio (individual non-linked)
kpis.def: Individual non-linked policies forfeited or lapsed during the year as a share of policies (IRDAI's lapse ratio).

kpis.name: Grievances per 10,000 policies
kpis.def: Grievances reported in the year per 10,000 individual policies in force.

kpis.name: Grievances resolved in the year
kpis.def: Grievances resolved divided by grievances open at start plus reported.

kpis.name: Ombudsman complaints per lakh policies
kpis.def: Complaints against the insurer received by the Insurance Ombudsman per 1,00,000 individual policies in force.
kpis.why: Escalations the insurer failed to resolve.

kpis.name: 13th-month persistency (by premium), latest disclosed
kpis.def: 13th-month persistency on premium basis from the insurer's latest disclosure.
kpis.why: The measure insurers report to investors.

pillars.name: Operating efficiency
pillars.question: How lean is the cost base?

kpis.name: Operating expense ratio
kpis.def: Operating expenses related to insurance business divided by premium.

kpis.name: Commission ratio
kpis.def: Commission paid divided by total premium.

kpis.name: Total cost ratio
kpis.def: Operating expenses plus commission, divided by premium.
kpis.why: All-in cost of acquiring and servicing business.

kpis.name: Commission ratio, 3-year change
kpis.def: Commission ratio now minus three years earlier, in percentage points.
kpis.why: Effect of the 2023 commission rules and channel competition.

kpis.name: Renewal share of total premium
kpis.def: Renewal premium as a share of total premium.

kpis.name: Total premium per office
kpis.def: Total premium divided by offices.

kpis.name: Operating expense per policy in force
kpis.def: Operating expenses divided by individual policies in force.
kpis.why: Unit servicing cost (affected by group business).

kpis.name: Benefits paid to premium
kpis.def: Benefits paid (claims, maturities, surrenders) divided by premium.
kpis.why: Maturity of the book and outflow pressure.

pillars.name: Digital & technology
pillars.question: How good are the digital touchpoints?

kpis.name: Android app rating
kpis.def: Google Play rating of the customer app.

kpis.name: iOS app rating
kpis.def: App Store rating of the customer app.

kpis.name: App rating, both stores
kpis.def: Average of Android and iOS ratings weighted by number of ratings.

kpis.name: Days since app update
kpis.def: Days since the Android app was last updated.

kpis.name: Homepage digital capabilities
kpis.def: Count of 12 capabilities found on the homepage: WhatsApp service, chat assistant, app links (Android, iOS), online premium payment, online claims, customer login, buy online, regional language, video KYC, UPI auto-pay, AI tools.
kpis.why: Breadth of the digital front door.

kpis.name: Online share of individual new business
kpis.def: Individual new business premium from online sales and web aggregators, share of total.

kpis.name: Homepage response time
kpis.def: Seconds to download the homepage HTML from a cloud server (mobile user agent).

pillars.name: People & organisation
pillars.question: How big, stable and productive is the organisation?

kpis.name: Employees
kpis.def: On-roll employees at year end (form L-45 or annual report).

kpis.name: Premium per employee
kpis.def: Total premium divided by employees.

kpis.name: Employee attrition
kpis.def: Employees who left during the year as a share of average headcount.

kpis.name: Women in workforce
kpis.def: Women as a share of employees (BRSR or annual report).

kpis.name: Agents per office
kpis.def: Individual agents divided by offices.

kpis.name: CEO tenure
kpis.def: Years since the current MD & CEO took office.

pillars.name: Governance, compliance & ESG
pillars.question: Is it well governed, well owned and clean with the regulator?

kpis.name: Listed on stock exchanges
kpis.def: Insurer's own shares listed on NSE/BSE.

kpis.name: Foreign shareholding
kpis.def: Foreign partner plus foreign portfolio holdings, where known.

kpis.name: Share price return, 1 year
kpis.def: One-year share price return for listed insurers (or listed holding company).

kpis.name: IRDAI penalties, 3 years
kpis.def: Penalty orders issued by IRDAI against the insurer in the last three years.

kpis.name: Independent directors on the board
kpis.def: Independent directors as a share of the board (form L-31).

pillars.name: Strategy & ambition
pillars.question: What is it trying to become?

bajaj.purpose: Group vision (Bajaj Finserv): to be a lifecycle partner to every Indian in achieving financial goals. Business construct for Bajaj Life: maximise customer benefits while gaining retail market share, keeping shareholder returns and growing value of new business.

pillars.name: Deep and wide distribution
pillars.detail: 598 branches; balanced mix of agency and institutional business including bancassurance; proprietary channel Bajaj Life Direct for up-selling and cross-selling; one of the largest private agency forces (164K+ agents).

pillars.name: Diversified product mix
pillars.detail: Balance of ULIP, traditional and group products, aiming for best-in-class features across need segments; rising protection share.

pillars.name: Operational efficiency
pillars.detail: Faster issuance and claim settlement, first-time-right processing, customer centricity.

pillars.name: Technology and data analytics
pillars.detail: Analytics as a differentiator for customers and sales partners; AI across the lifecycle (enablement, login, underwriting, claims, servicing).

targets.text: Grow retail topline at about 2x the industry and keep gaining private-sector market share (retail weighted received premium share 7.9% in FY26 against 8.6% in FY24).
Raise protection to about 10% of business (4% in FY24, 8% in FY26).
Product mix of about 10% protection, 25% non-par, 30% par and 35% ULIP (FY26 traditional:ULIP 57:43).
Return on embedded value of 18-20% (14.1% in FY26).
Value of new business growing much faster than premium (new business margin 19.2% in FY26, up from 15% in FY24).

bajaj.parentage: Wholly owned by the Bajaj group (Bajaj Finserv with Bajaj Holdings & Investment) after Allianz SE's exit in 2025-26; renamed from Bajaj Allianz Life.

sources.title: Bajaj Finserv investor presentation, Q1 FY27 (Bajaj Life section)

hdfc.purpose: Build a resilient, technology-driven and scalable business, with digital, paperless journeys across channels.

pillars.name: Profitable growth
pillars.detail: Sustainable growth by finding and tapping new profit pools; VNB and EV compounding.

pillars.name: Diversified distribution mix
pillars.detail: Multiple channels to drive need-based selling and deepen penetration: agency, bancassurance, non-bank alliances and direct. Agency expanding to 700+ branches, 80% of new branches in Tier 2/3 markets.

pillars.name: Customer first
pillars.detail: Superior product propositions and customer journeys through consistent innovation.

pillars.name: Risk management and board governance
pillars.detail: Risk focus guided by an independent, competent board.

pillars.name: Future-ready organisation (foundation)
pillars.detail: Technology, digital and analytics; organisation-wide AI programme across new business operations, servicing, distribution and risk.

key_facts: H1 FY27: individual APE Rs 70.8 bn (+9%), VNB Rs 20.4 bn (+12%), new business margin 24.7%, PAT Rs 11.2 bn (+14%), AUM Rs 4,097 bn.
Overall market share grew from 7.5% (FY18) to 10.8% (FY26) per the company.
hdfc.parentage: Listed; promoted by HDFC Bank. Exide Life merged into HDFC Life in 2022.

sources.title: HDFC Life investor presentation, H1 FY27

sbi.purpose: Make insurance accessible to all through an extensive national presence, driven by a 'Customer-First' approach, world-class operating efficiency and hassle-free claims.

pillars.name: Sustainable growth and penetration
pillars.detail: Strengthen distribution and expand insurance penetration (management statement, H1 FY27).

pillars.name: Protection-led, diversified portfolio
pillars.detail: Customer-centric solutions, protection-led offerings and a diversified product portfolio (APE mix par/non-par/ULIP 4/45/51 in H1 FY27).

pillars.name: Operating efficiency
pillars.detail: Among the lowest cost ratios in the industry (total cost ratio 11.7% in H1 FY27).

pillars.name: Digital experience
pillars.detail: Enhance digital experiences for customers, distributors and employees.

key_facts: H1 FY27: private market leader in individual new business premium (25.2% share) and individual rated premium (22.6%).
APE Rs 117.5 bn (+18%); VoNB Rs 32.7 bn (+19%); VoNB margin 27.9%; PAT Rs 12.7 bn (+17%); operating RoEV 18.8%; solvency 1.97; AUM Rs 5.3 trillion.
sbi.parentage: Listed; promoted by State Bank of India. Took over Sahara India Life's policies in 2023.

sources.title: SBI Life news release, H1 FY27 results (27 Oct 2026)

absli.parentage: Part of Aditya Birla Capital (listed NBFC holding company); 51:49 joint venture of the Aditya Birla Group and Sun Life Financial (Canada). Incorporated August 2000, operating since January 2001.

tataaia.purpose: Aligned to the Tata Group core purpose of improving the quality of life of the communities it serves through long-term stakeholder value creation, and to AIA's aim of 'Healthier, Longer, Better' lives.
tataaia.parentage: Joint venture of Tata Sons and AIA Group (pan-Asian life insurer in 18 markets).

pnbmetlife.purpose: Insurance solutions across child education, family protection, long-term savings and retirement, sold largely through bank partnerships and a financial advisor force.
pnbmetlife.parentage: MetLife with Punjab National Bank and other shareholders; key bank partners PNB, Jammu & Kashmir Bank and Karnataka Bank. MD & CEO Sameer Bansal.

indiafirst.purpose: A #CustomerFirst ideology and a 'Circle of Trust' proposition: every behaviour aimed at earning customer trust, delivered through digitalisation across the value chain.

shriram.purpose: Stated purpose: bring every family, especially those most vulnerable to losing a breadwinner, into the safety net of life insurance.
values: High-quality, cost-effective solutions for the average Indian
shriram.parentage: Part of the Shriram Group, founded in 1974 by R. Thyagarajan.

indusindnippon.purpose: Stated purpose: to be a trusted partner who empowers every individual to be ready for every stage of life.
indusindnippon.parentage: IndusInd International Holdings (IIHL) with Nippon Life; renamed from Reliance Nippon Life in December 2025.

pramerica.purpose: Trusted guidance on life insurance for individuals and groups through multiple distribution channels.

bharti.purpose: 'Customer First' as a core value: value-for-money, need-based insurance with a hassle-free experience.
bharti.parentage: Held by Bharti Life Ventures Pvt Ltd after AXA's exit; renamed Bharti Life Insurance in September 2025.

edelweiss.purpose: Mission to turn customers' goals into reality; cost-effective operations and a customer's-eye view of every product, service point and claim.
edelweiss.parentage: Joint venture of Edelweiss Financial Services and Tokio Marine Holdings (Japan).

bandhan.purpose: Make life insurance affordable, accessible and simple, using technology to streamline everything from plan selection to claims; customers at the heart of everything.
bandhan.parentage: Bandhan Financial Holdings (Bandhan group); formerly Aegon Life, established 2008.

aviva.purpose: Stated purpose: 'With you today, for a better tomorrow'.
aviva.parentage: Wholly owned subsidiary of Aviva International Holdings (Aviva plc, London-listed).

acko.purpose: Mission: empower people with reliable protection for peace of mind and lasting prosperity; digital-first, direct-to-customer model.
acko.parentage: Part of the ACKO group founded by Varun Dua.

lic.parentage: Government of India owns the large majority; listed on NSE/BSE since May 2022.

icici.parentage: Listed; promoted by ICICI Bank. Renamed from ICICI Prudential Life to ICICI Life Insurance with effect from 22 Sep 2026 (IRDAI).

axismax.parentage: Max Financial Services (listed) with Axis Bank as co-promoter.

kotak.parentage: Wholly owned by Kotak Mahindra Bank.

canarahsbc.parentage: Canara Bank with HSBC Insurance; listed on NSE/BSE.

sud.parentage: Bank of India, Union Bank of India and Dai-ichi Life (Japan).

generalicentral.parentage: Generali (Italy) with Central Bank of India; renamed from Future Generali India Life in July 2025.

godigit.parentage: Part of the Go Digit group.

creditaccess.parentage: Part of the CreditAccess group (microfinance); business is mainly group and credit-life cover.

sahara.parentage: Under administration; policies transferred to SBI Life by IRDAI order (June 2023).

indiapost.parentage: Department of Posts, Government of India (Postal Life Insurance and Rural PLI), outside IRDAI.

strategy_meta.note: Strategy profiles. 'stated' items come from the insurer's own website, annual report or investor presentation (paraphrased, with short quotes marked). The app adds a data view computed from the KPIs. Status: deep = pillars and targets from an investor deck; partial = purpose, values and footprint from the website; pending = not yet researched.
